name: Question 2
problem: What is the coefficient of ${(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{4}?$
worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(\frac{\pi }{4})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4})(x-\frac{\pi }{4})+\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}){(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of ${(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is 

$$
\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}).
$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4})=-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of ${(x-\frac{\pi }{4})}^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

What is the coefficient of (x−π4)2 in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x)=sin⁡x at x=π4?

a
−2
b
−42
c
−24
d
22
e
28
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The second-degree Taylor polynomial of f(x) about x=π4 is given by

P2(x)=f(π4)+f′(π4)(x−π4)+12f″(π4)(x−π4)2.

The coefficient of (x−π4)2 in the above Taylor polynomial is 12f″(π4).

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative f″(x):

f(x)=sin⁡xf′(x)=cos⁡xf″(x)=−sin⁡x

Then, we evaluate f″(x) at x=π4. This gives

f″(π4)=−sin⁡(π4)=−22.

Finally, we determine the coefficient of (x−π4)2, as follows:

12f″(π4)=12⋅(−22)=−24
